source_review.notes: Reviewed PostgreSQL 18 file/page/FSM/system-column documentation, SQL Server heap documentation, MySQL 8.4 clustered-index documentation, Oracle Database 23 concepts, and the two cited database-systems textbooks. All seven online official destinations returned HTTP 200 after replacing an invalid Oracle HTML path with the official versioned PDF. Heap, RID/ctid, forwarding, free-space, and clustered-storage claims are scoped by engine.

evidence: Checked relation pages P_i, count N, capacities C_i, data bytes D_i, metadata M_i, reusable bytes F_i, scan page/byte formulas, and contextual RID notation.
Checked separation of logical visits, physical reads, output cardinality, cache residency, and elapsed time.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The formulas are simplified cost/capacity models rather than vendor implementation guarantees.

evidence: Recomputed A/B and C/D page usage as 94 bytes with six free on each page.
Recomputed B deletion as page-0 usage 44/free 56 and E slot reuse as usage 89/free 11.
Recomputed F(95) plus two-byte slot as 97 bytes on a new page with three free.
Recomputed the 10000 by 8192-byte scan as 81920000 logical bytes and 16384000 expected cold bytes under the stated 80-percent residency simplification.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No elapsed-time, cache-independence, engine density, or production I/O claim is inferred.

evidence: Re-derived retained slot overhead in page used/free calculations and reusable-slot insertion.
Re-derived the logical O(N) page consideration for exhaustive heap predicates without a ruling-out access path.
Re-derived why aggregate relation free bytes do not imply one row fits a page.
Re-derived RID reuse as a counterexample to durable physical identity.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The scan argument permits valid page-skipping summaries/indexes and does not equate logical visits with physical device operations.

evidence: Reviewed empty/full relations, exact fits, slot overhead, aggregate-but-not-local free space, stale selection hints, concurrent extension, short writes, and full storage.
Reviewed free/normal/forwarded/invisible slots, RID/page reuse, relation generation changes, malformed/checksum-failed pages, overflow, and forwarding cycles.
Reviewed MVCC retention, long snapshots, index-to-heap mismatch, aborted/dead versions, delete versus truncation, and correlation decay.
Reviewed interrupted maintenance, headroom including indexes/logs/snapshots, cancellation, replicas, backup/restore, failover, and irreversible rewrite boundaries.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Byte-level inspection is restricted to supported tools or protected, version-matched copies.

evidence: Validated every modeled page remains within its 100-byte capacity and every slot size is nonnegative.
Validated first-fit placement, retained slot accounting, free-slot reuse, physical scan enumeration, and relation extension.
Validated scan matches D/F by stored size while visiting all three pages.
The repository verifier matched exact ten-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status.
invariant_checking.notes: The model omits bytes, schema, indexes, visibility, concurrency, space maps, WAL, checksums, and recovery.

evidence: Reviewed each first-fit decision against tuple size plus conditional slot cost.
Reviewed page usage/free conservation through insert, delete, reuse, and extension.
Reviewed adversarial completeness reasoning for a predicate without a usable page/index exclusion mechanism.
Reviewed RID lifetime counterexample after delete and slot reuse.
proof_review.notes: No universal page-selection complexity, RID format/lifetime, scan optimizer behavior, or transaction correctness proof is claimed.

evidence: Separated database heap from binary/memory heaps and heap organization from clustered/index-organized storage.
Separated physical page order, insertion chronology, and SQL ordering guarantees.
Separated reusable space, reclaimable dead bytes, relation shrinkage, and OS allocation.
Separated structural presence from snapshot visibility and logical page visits from physical reads.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Unordered, free, live, stable, full, scanned, reclaimed, and verified claims name their layer and assumptions.

evidence: The standard-library heap placement/scan model executed successfully through the repository verifier.
All seven online official reference destinations returned HTTP 200 on 2026-08-30.
Front matter, exact section order, local links, ten examples, five exercises, five answers, and snippet expectations passed draft validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live heap, index, MVCC snapshot, forwarding chain, free-space map, extension/truncation, rewrite, fault, backup/restore, or performance workload was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently treats a heap as an unordered but highly structured relation organization governed by page, tuple, visibility, locator, index, allocation, and recovery contracts.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed selection, insertion, extension, RIDs, scans, visibility, deletion, updates/forwarding, index maintenance, clustered contrasts, correlation, fragmentation, maintenance, observability, inspection, capacity, replicas, and backup/restore.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet, executable heap lifecycle, ten distinct cost/correctness/operations examples, and five progressive exercises support self-study from placement arithmetic through production reclamation design.

limitations: Internal authoring, official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model do not certify any PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle, MySQL/InnoDB, or other live heap/clustered format, RID lifetime, page-selection policy, MVCC state, index consistency, scan performance, maintenance outcome, backup/restore, fault recovery, or production fitness.
